drafted_from: tool row in tools/office-files/tool-rows.json, do-work/decode-office-open-xml.py and test/decode-office-open-xml.test.py (run on its fixture)
start_here: Say to your AI: "Read /work/budget.xlsx and show me every cell, including the formulas I typed." It reads the tool's row, then runs decode-office-open-xml.py on your computer and tells you what the sheets hold.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it reads or rewrites one file on the person's own computer and prints what it found or changed.
instructions: 1. Say which xlsx, docx or pptx file to read (for a long sheet add --sheet NAME or --max-rows N).
2. The AI reads the row with tools:list {tool: tool:read-an-office-file} and runs its `run` command from the Workshop checkout; add --formulas to see what was typed in each cell.

3. Read the one JSON object it prints: kind (workbook, document, presentation or container) and sheets with rows of cells, blocks of paragraphs (selector paragraph:N) and tables, or slides in the deck's own order.
4. Tell the person what the file holds in their words; to change it use tool:change-cells-or-words-in-an-office-file.

worked_examples.title: Read a one-sheet workbook with its formulas
worked_examples.ask: Read /work/budget.xlsx and show me every cell, including the formulas I typed.
worked_examples.given: From tools/office-files/test/decode-office-open-xml.test.py, which builds this workbook; I ran its decoder on that fixture to observe the output. Command: python3 -I tools/office-files/do-work/decode-office-open-xml.py /work/budget.xlsx --formulas. The workbook has one sheet, Model, with A1 "Runway (months)", B1 "Price is $2,499 per seat", A2 12 and B2 the formula IF(A2>0,999,A2) showing 999.
worked_examples.hands_back: {"kind":"workbook","sheets":[{"name":"Model","rows":[{"row":1,"cells":{"A":{"value":"Runway (months)"},"B":{"value":"Price is $2,499 per seat"}}},{"row":2,"cells":{"A":{"value":12},"B":{"value":999,"formula":"IF(A2>0,999,A2)"}}}]}]} Without --formulas, B2 comes back as {"value":999} alone.
